title: Peperonata Rossa
subtitle: Slow-cooked red peppers and tomatoes with garlic and basil
excerpt: Sweet red peppers collapsed into jammy softness with tomatoes, garlic, and olive oil. Serve warm as a side dish or at room temperature on bread.
sourceNotes: Classic Italian peperonata from southern and central Italian cooking traditions.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in a sealed container for up to 3 months. Defrost at room temperature and reheat gently.
recipe.batchNotes: Scales easily. Use your largest pan and cook in a single layer so the peppers colour rather than steam.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Tastes better the next day once the flavours settle. Keep in the fridge and serve warm or at room temperature.

content.text: Peperonata is all about patience. Cook the peppers low and slow until they are completely soft and sweet. Do not rush the heat or they will catch before they collapse. The finished dish should look glossy and saucy.
Heat the olive oil in a wide pan over a medium-low heat. Add the onion and cook for 8 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and cook for 2 minutes. Do not let it colour.
Add all the pepper strips and stir to coat in the oil. Season with salt and pepper. Cook on a low heat for 15 minutes, stirring now and then.
Pour in the tinned tomatoes. Break them up with a spoon. Stir to combine.
Cook uncovered on a low heat for 25 minutes until the peppers are very soft and the sauce has thickened.
Add the red wine vinegar if using. Stir through the basil. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Serve warm or at room temperature.

items.symptom: The peppers are sticking to the pan.
items.cause: The heat is too high or there is not enough oil.
items.fix: Turn the heat to low and add a splash of water to loosen everything.

items.symptom: The sauce is too watery after cooking.
items.cause: The peppers released a lot of liquid and the lid was left on.
items.fix: Cook uncovered for a further 10 minutes on a slightly higher heat to reduce the liquid.

items.cause: They were cooked too quickly on a high heat.
items.fix: Peperonata needs a very low, patient cook. If they taste bitter, add a pinch of sugar and continue on low heat.
